name: Artificial Analysis: independent AI model and API provider benchmarks
title: Artificial Analysis: independent AI model and API provider benchmarks
answer: Artificial Analysis publishes this landing page for its comparison of AI models and API hosting providers, benchmarked independently on quality, price, output speed and latency. Its most useful contribution here is the definition of its metrics, including pass^5 reliability on AA-AnalystAgent, the cost of running its Intelligence Index, and endpoint accuracy preservation. The harvested text does not mention healthcare, medical reasoning or clinical tasks, so it does not itself support a claim that models are ranked on medical work.

sections.body: This is the landing page of Artificial Analysis, published by Artificial Analysis itself, described as comparison and analysis of AI models and API hosting providers, with independent benchmarks across key performance metrics including quality, price, output speed and latency. It is not a report or a study but a front page that introduces the site's benchmarking work and defines the terms used in its comparisons. The text was harvested on 26 September 2026. No author, publication date or revision date is stated in the text, and no funding or ownership details appear.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page lists model developers including Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta, Google, DeepSeek, Mistral, Alibaba, NVIDIA, Xiaomi, MiniMax, Kimi, StepFun, Z AI, Thinking Machines and the Institute of Foundation Models, and hosting providers including Amazon, Azure, Google Vertex, Groq, Cerebras, Together AI, SambaNova, CoreWeave, Crusoe, DeepInfra, Nebius, Novita, Parasail, Scaleway and Baseten. The substance in the harvested text is a set of metric definitions. Model weights are labelled Commercial Use Restricted where commercial use is limited by conditions, and Non-commercial where the licence prohibits commercial use. AA-AnalystAgent is described as a benchmark for end-to-end quantitative analysis on real-world spreadsheets and documents, with every question run five independent times, so pass^5 measures how reliably a model reproduces a correct answer rather than how often it reaches one. The cost figure covers running the evaluations in the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, calculated from input, cache hit, cache write, reasoning and answer token prices and the tokens used. Tokens per second is measured after the first chunk is received. A provider endpoint score is a composite of how much of a model's accuracy an endpoint preserves, from re-running BFCL v4-500, HLE-250 and AA-LCR-25, expressed as a percentage of a self-hosted reference where one exists. The page notes that while model intelligence generally translates across use cases, specific evaluations may be more relevant for certain use cases.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The text gives no healthcare or medical figures. It states that AA-AnalystAgent questions are run five independent times, that endpoint accuracy is measured by re-running BFCL v4-500, HLE-250 and AA-LCR-25, and that a score of 100 means an endpoint matches the self-hosted reference. It states that endpoint scores are point-in-time snapshots, and that models are labelled Commercial Use Restricted or Non-commercial according to their licence terms.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in healthcare would use this source to compare models and hosting endpoints on general quality, price, output speed, latency and accuracy preservation, and to understand how Artificial Analysis defines reliability, which matters when a model must reproduce a correct answer rather than reach one occasionally. The text contains no medical benchmarks, no clinical tasks and no healthcare data, so it cannot be used to show which model performs best on medical reasoning. The claim that Artificial Analysis ranks models on medical tasks is not evidenced by this harvested text.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Healthcare

sections.body: This is a landing page, and the harvested text is largely navigation, provider lists and metric definitions, with no actual scores or rankings. It does not cover healthcare, clinical validation, regulation or patient data. No publication date, author or methodology detail beyond brief definitions is given, and the text does not state how the site is funded, so its independence is asserted rather than demonstrated here. It is a partial snapshot of a site that changes over time.
